gaps: No editing tutorial specific to Bihari/Patna/Mithila weddings (matkor, kohbar, sindoor-daan night pheras): every result is pan-Indian or Western.

No video colour tutorial on mixed lighting at Indian night weddings (tungsten plus LED stage washes, coloured baraat lights, fireworks). Searches returned only photo-editing (Lightroom) or on-set lighting setups, so night handling relies on generic low-light and denoise videos.
No tutorial on cleaning or mixing live group folk singing (women singing geet or gaali with dholak) in a noisy room. Audio cleanup results are all single-voice dialogue denoise.

Hindi Final Cut Pro wedding colour is thin. Lakshay Bagga's FCP Hindi grade is only 6 min, and AtomX UHD covers editing more than colour. Indian Hindi colour tutorials with real depth are DaVinci or Premiere.

No Final Cut Pro tutorial on structuring a 1-3 hour traditional full-length master film (ritual-by-ritual chaptering, song beds per ritual). Hindi 'shaadi mixing' tutorials mostly use Edius; AtomX UHD's FCP video is the closest.

Video shot selection for Indian weddings: John Bunn (Western, Premiere) and the Cinemasters full-edit chapters are the only sources. No tutorial ranks Indian ritual moments (e.g. which jaymala or sindoor-daan angles to keep).

In this run YouTube asked for a sign-in on every per-video detail fetch, so the newly added picks (-SJRRFQvA54, mLtqqXHtD1Q, olf55HAiV9s, CFvGPBE22yM, 5z5OrQzqrJc, _kaUMcG48Gc) were judged on title, channel, length and views only. Their descriptions and chapters were not checked.
